title: model-bindings.v1 — capability-tier → model/effort bindings for engine personas
description: The single committed file that maps a persona's capability tier (model-tier: judgment or mechanical — the name-free demand vocabulary the personas already declare) to the model alias and reasoning effort that realize it, with per-persona overrides. This is how the engine selects models without naming a model in any persona file: personas stay capability-shaped, and which model realizes a tier is the evolving judgment kept HERE, in one place, so retuning for a new model landscape is one file edit re-rendered across every persona. Model values are durable aliases only (opus, sonnet, fable, …), never a versioned id that rots — the pattern rejects digits so a pinned dated id cannot be committed, while the engine names no closed set of aliases (a new model is adopted by changing a value, never the grammar). The per-persona overrides express a mixed-by-lens scheme — a deep or adversarial lens on a stronger model, a systematic lens a tier down — as the operator's tuning. Retuning is the operator's own act: edit this file and re-run agent_bindings.py render.

schema_version.description: Which version of this file's shape this is. Today the only valid value is 1.

tiers.description: The default binding for each capability tier. Both tiers are always present: judgment (careful reasoning) and mechanical (bounded work). A persona with no override inherits its tier's binding.

overrides.description: Per-persona bindings, keyed by the persona's name (its .claude/agents/<name>.md slug). An override wins over the persona's tier default — this is how a specific lens is tuned to a stronger or cheaper model without changing its declared capability tier. A key that names no installed persona is a stale override, caught by the agent-bindings coherence test.

implementation_classes.description: Per-provider model/effort bindings for the DAG Build's DISPATCHED worker classes — the source of truth the coordinator renders into a worker's route and into the worker personas. This is a SEPARATE axis from the review `tiers`: reviewer personas resolve a name-free demand tier (judgment|mechanical) to one model, while a dispatched worker resolves its implementation class (builder|bounded) to a per-PROVIDER model+effort, because Claude and Codex realize the same class with different frontier/efficient models. The `integrator` class is never dispatched (it is the current senior session, so it carries no fixed binding here). A worker model alias MAY carry digits/dots (a provider-native family name like gpt-5.6-terra), so it uses its own grammar — the review `binding` anti-rot pattern is deliberately left untouched. Optional: a deployment with no DAG worker packs need not declare it.

review_depths.description: The per-depth reviewer EFFORT the operator's review-depth choice scales — the single depth dial (StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#677). Each present depth carries ONE effort applied uniformly to the reviewers that depth runs; there is deliberately NO model dimension here, because depth scales effort (thoroughness/token spend) while MODEL stays matched per-lens to each lens's nature via `tiers`+`overrides`, stable across depths — stepping both at once would double-cut the middle tier toward Quick. `quick` carries no entry (it runs no cold reviewers). `thorough` is the anchor (high, so it is a zero-regression identity with today's stamped effort); `standard` steps effort down. On Claude the depth effort is realized by the session --effort governing the un-pinned reviewer roles; on Codex by spawning each cold reviewer as a non-full-history fork (fork_turns="none") with reasoning_effort set from the depth (the un-pinned twin bakes no model_reasoning_effort). Optional: absent, the depth passes no effort, so reviewers run at their un-pinned default (Claude Code's session default; the Codex fork carries none). Operators retune these values through the preserved operator-review-effort override, which survives an engine update.

binding.description: One model + effort pairing that realizes a capability demand.

model.description: A durable model alias — lowercase letters and hyphens only, NO digits, so a versioned id that rots (claude-opus-4-20250101) cannot be committed while any durable alias (opus, sonnet, haiku, fable) is accepted. The engine names no closed set of aliases.

effort.description: The reasoning-effort level that, with the model, realizes the tier. A bounded platform concept.

implementation_binding.description: One implementation class's bindings, one per provider. Both providers are present so a class renders explicitly for Claude and Codex from a single source, rather than one provider silently inheriting a frontier default.

provider_binding.description: One provider-native model + effort pairing for a dispatched worker class. Unlike the review `binding`, the model alias MAY carry digits/dots so a provider-native family name (gpt-5.6-terra) is expressible; it remains an operator-tunable alias, not a dated snapshot id.

model.description: A provider-native model alias — lowercase alphanumerics separated by hyphen or dot (e.g. sonnet, haiku, gpt-5.6-terra). Digits are permitted here, unlike the review binding grammar.

effort.description: The reasoning-effort level for this worker class.

depth_effort.description: One review depth's reasoning effort — the single value the depth applies to the reviewers it runs. No model dimension (model stays the per-lens tiers+overrides at every depth). The enum is the review effort range; xhigh/max are deliberately not offered here — the three depths need no more, and holding to low/medium/high keeps the value valid as a Codex model_reasoning_effort too.

effort.description: The reasoning-effort level this depth runs its reviewers at.
